blueprint.name: Common Law Admission Test
blueprint.source: CLAT: 120 questions, 120 marks, 120 minutes; negative 0.25. Section counts vary by year, so this split is provisional.

questions.text: In a contract for the supply of 500 tonnes of steel, Party A agreed to deliver the steel by 1st June. Due to a sudden strike by steelworkers, the supply was delayed until 15th June. Party B sued for damages for delay. Which doctrine will most likely relieve Party A from liability?

options.label: A
options.text: Doctrine of frustration of contract

options.label: B
options.text: Doctrine of impossibility of performance

options.label: C
options.text: Doctrine of force majeure

options.label: D
options.text: Doctrine of anticipatory breach

questions.solution: Shortcut: Identify the clause that specifically deals with external events beyond control. - Frustration applies when the contract becomes impossible, not merely delayed. - Impossibility also requires total impossibility. - Anticipatory breach involves a clear intention not to perform. - Force majeure covers temporary impediments like strikes. Hence option C is correct. Full solution: A strike is a recognized force majeure event that temporarily prevents performance but does not render the contract impossible. Under standard force majeure clauses, Party A is excused from liability for the delay caused by the strike.

questions.text: With reference to the G20 New Delhi Leaders' Declaration adopted in September 2023, which of the following statements is correct regarding the African Union's status?

options.label: A
options.text: A. The African Union was admitted as a permanent member of the G20, equivalent to the European Union.

options.label: B
options.text: B. The African Union was granted 'Guest Invitee' status for the 2023 summit only.

options.label: C
options.text: C. The African Union was admitted as a permanent member but without voting rights on financial regulations.

options.label: D
options.text: D. The African Union's membership was deferred pending a review of the AU's institutional capacity.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate options suggesting temporary status (B), conditional rights (C), or deferral (D) — the historic outcome was full permanent membership. Worked Solution: The G20 New Delhi Leaders' Declaration (Sept 9, 2023) formally admitted the African Union as a permanent member of the G20, granting it the same status as the European Union, marking a significant shift towards greater Global South representation.

questions.text: What is the unit digit of the product (7^95 × 3^58)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use cyclicity of unit digits. For 7: cycle is 7, 9, 3, 1 (length 4). 95 ÷ 4 leaves remainder 3 → 3rd digit = 3. For 3: cycle is 3, 9, 7, 1 (length 4). 58 ÷ 4 leaves remainder 2 → 2nd digit = 9. Multiply unit digits: 3 × 9 = 27 → unit digit 7. Step-by-step: 7^95 unit digit = 7^(4×23+3) → (7^4)^23 × 7^3 → 1^23 × 343 → 3. 3^58 unit digit = 3^(4×14+2) → (3^4)^14 × 3^2 → 1^14 × 9 → 9. Product unit digit = 3 × 9 = 27 → 7.

questions.text: The Constitution (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment) Act, 2023, which provides for one-third reservation of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies, stipulates that the reservation shall cease to exist after a specific period unless extended by Parliament. What is the duration specified in the Act for the continuation of this reservation provision?

options.label: A
options.text: 15 years from the date of commencement

options.label: B
options.text: 25 years from the date of commencement

options.label: C
options.text: 30 years from the date of commencement

options.label: D
options.text: 50 years from the date of commencement

questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate options based on standard constitutional amendment durations for reservations (e.g., SC/ST reservation was 10 years, often extended). The 106th Amendment specifically uses a 15-year sunset clause (Article 334A), distinct from the 25/30-year distractors. Full Solution: The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023 (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam) inserted Article 334A. It mandates that the reservation of seats for women in the House of the People and State Legislative Assemblies shall cease to have effect on the expiration of a period of 15 years from the date of commencement of the Act, unless Parliament extends it by law.

questions.text: The Constitution (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment) Act, 2023 (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam) provides for reservation of one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies. Which of the following statements accurately describes a key condition for its implementation?

options.label: A
options.text: It comes into force immediately upon Presidential assent.

options.label: B
options.text: It requires ratification by at least half of the State Legislatures.

options.label: C
options.text: It shall come into effect after the publication of the first Census conducted after its commencement.

options.label: D
options.text: It is subject to a mandatory review by the Supreme Court before notification.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Constitutional amendments changing federal structure (delimitation) need Census data. Option C mentions 'first Census after commencement' - standard trigger for delimitation-based reservations. Worked Solution: Article 334A inserted by the 106th Amendment explicitly states the reservation comes into effect after the delimitation exercise following the first Census after the Act's commencement (expected post-2026 Census). It did not require state ratification (not altering State List/Representation in RS) nor immediate commencement.

questions.text: Premises: (1) Every claim that is verified is reliable. (2) Some reliable statements are unverified. (3) No unverified claim is false. Which of the following must be true?

options.label: A
options.text: All verified claims are true.

options.label: B
options.text: Some verified claims are unverified.

options.label: C
options.text: Some reliable statements are false.

options.label: D
options.text: No verified claim is false.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Combine the universal statements to see the relationship between verified and false. From (1) verified → reliable. From (3) unverified → ¬false (i.e., unverified claims are not false). Since every verified claim is reliable, and any claim that is not false must be true, we can infer that no verified claim is false. Full solution: (1) ∀x (Verified(x) → Reliable(x)). (3) ∀x (Unverified(x) → ¬False(x)). A verified claim cannot be unverified, so it is not covered by (3). However, if a claim were false, it would contradict (3) because false claims are necessarily verified (otherwise they'd be unverified and not false). Hence a verified claim cannot be false, establishing that no verified claim is false. Options A, B, and C either overstate or contradict the premises.

questions.text: The three new criminal laws—the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA)—replaced the IPC, CrPC, and Indian Evidence Act respectively. From which specific date did these laws come into effect across India?

options.label: A
options.text: January 26, 2024

options.label: B
options.text: July 1, 2024

options.label: C
options.text: August 15, 2024

options.label: D
options.text: October 2, 2024

questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate symbolic national dates (Republic Day, Independence Day, Gandhi Jayanti) used as distractors; the Gazette notification specified a mid-year administrative date. Worked Solution: The Ministry of Home Affairs issued separate notifications in February 2024 appointing July 1, 2024, as the date on which the provisions of the BNS, BNSS, and BSA would come into force, replacing the colonial-era statutes.

questions.text: The table below lists three statutes and the year they were enacted. A petition challenges a provision of one of these statutes on the ground that it violates the doctrine of "pith and substance". Which statute is most likely to be upheld as a valid exercise of State legislative power? Statute | Subject | Year Enacted ---|---|--- A | Regulation of water supply within a municipality | 2019 B | Grant of licences for mining of minerals in a district | 2020 C | Imposition of a tax on inter-state sale of goods | 2021

options.label: A
options.text: Statute A

options.label: B
options.text: Statute B

options.label: C
options.text: Statute C

options.label: D
options.text: All of the above

questions.solution: Shortcut: Identify the entry list – water supply and mining are in State List, inter‑state tax is Union List. Hence only B (mining) is clearly within State competence. Full solution: Under the Seventh Schedule, "Regulation of water supply" falls under Entry 17 (State List) and is valid. "Grant of licences for mining" is Entry 23 (State List) and also valid. "Imposition of tax on inter‑state sale of goods" falls under Entry 92 (Union List) and is beyond State power, so the provision would be struck down. Since the question asks which is most likely to be upheld, the safest answer is Statute B, as it is unmistakably within State power without any overlapping Union competence.

rows: Regulation of water supply within a municipality
Grant of licences for mining of minerals in a district
Imposition of a tax on inter‑state sale of goods

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'BRAIN' is written as 'CSBJO'. How will 'HEART' be written in that code?

options.label: A
options.text: IFBSV

options.label: B
options.text: IFBSU

options.label: C
options.text: IGFSU

options.label: D
options.text: JFBSU

questions.solution: Shortcut: Each letter in the code is the immediate next letter in the alphabet (+1). Apply the same shift to every letter of HEART. Step‑by‑step: H→I, E→F, A→B, R→S, T→U, giving IFBSU.

questions.text: Arrange the following sentences in the most logical order to form a coherent paragraph: 1. The experiment was conducted over a period of six months. 2. Researchers collected data on plant growth under varying light conditions. 3. The results indicated a significant correlation between light intensity and growth rate. 4. Based on these findings, the team recommended further studies on spectral quality.
questions.solution: Shortcut: The opening sentence must introduce the experiment's duration (sentence 1). Only option D begins with sentence 1. Verify the flow: 1 (timeframe) → 2 (data collection) → 3 (results) → 4 (recommendation). Full solution: Sentence 1 sets the temporal context. Sentence 2 describes the methodology. Sentence 3 reports the findings. Sentence 4 draws a conclusion and suggests further research. Option D (1-2-3-4) is the only sequence that follows this logical progression.

questions.text: Arrange the following sentences in the most logical sequence to form a coherent paragraph. 1. However, the economic benefits of such projects are often overstated. 2. Mega-infrastructure projects are frequently touted as engines of national growth. 3. Independent audits reveal that cost overruns average 40% and ridership shortfalls exceed 50%. 4. Consequently, the financial burden inevitably shifts to the taxpayer.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Identify the Opening Sentence (general statement, no contrast/conclusion markers). Sentence 2 introduces the topic. Sentence 1 ('However') must immediately follow a positive claim (Sentence 2). Sentence 3 ('Independent audits reveal') provides evidence for the claim in Sentence 1. Sentence 4 ('Consequently') concludes the causal chain. Sequence 2-1-3-4 is the only logical flow.

questions.text: A citizen files a petition under Article 32 of the Constitution challenging the constitutional validity of a State law that imposes a tax on the sale of agricultural produce within the State. The petition claims that the tax violates the fundamental right to trade and commerce under Article 19(1)(g). Which of the following is the most appropriate ground for the Court to reject the petition?

options.label: A
options.text: The tax is a reasonable restriction in the public interest and therefore permissible under Article 19(6).

options.label: B
options.text: The petition is not maintainable as the aggrieved party has not suffered a direct injury.

options.label: C
options.text: Article 32 does not entertain challenges to State legislation, only to Central legislation.

options.label: D
options.text: The tax is a fiscal measure and cannot be challenged on the ground of violation of fundamental rights.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate options that are factually incorrect. 1. Article 19(6) allows reasonable restrictions, but the petition is about validity, not restriction. 2. Under Article 32, any person whose rights are infringed can file; direct injury is required – the petitioner must show personal impact. 3. Article 32 can be invoked against any law violating fundamental rights, irrespective of its origin. 4. Fiscal measures can be challenged if they infringe rights. Hence option B is the correct ground for rejection. Full solution: The petitioner must demonstrate that he is directly affected by the tax; mere public interest standing is insufficient. Since the petition lacks a specific personal grievance, the Court can dismiss it on the basis of lack of locus standi.

questions.text: Argument: The city council proposes to ban plastic bags to reduce litter. Opponents argue that paper bags have a larger carbon footprint. Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the council's proposal?

options.label: A
options.text: Plastic bags take 500 years to decompose.

options.label: B
options.text: Many shoppers already bring reusable bags.

options.label: C
options.text: Paper bags are biodegradable but require more energy to produce.

options.label: D
options.text: A study shows plastic bag bans reduce overall plastic waste by 70%.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Look for evidence that directly supports the proposal's effectiveness in reducing litter/waste. Option D provides empirical data showing the ban achieves its goal. Option A is a fact about plastic but doesn't address the ban's impact. Option B is irrelevant to the ban's efficacy. Option C actually weakens by highlighting a drawback of alternatives. Step-by-step: 1) Identify the proposal's goal: reduce litter. 2) Evaluate each option for direct support of that goal. 3) Discard options that are tangential or counterproductive. 4) Choose the option with concrete evidence of success.

questions.text: A driver was charged under Section 304A IPC for causing death by negligence. The prosecution's case rests solely on the testimony of a surviving passenger who states that the driver was texting while driving. The defense moves to exclude this testimony on the ground that it is hearsay. How should the court rule?

options.label: A
options.text: Exclude the testimony as it is hearsay and not within any exception.

options.label: B
options.text: Admit the testimony because the passenger is a party to the case.

options.label: C
options.text: Admit the testimony as a dying declaration.

options.label: D
options.text: Admit the testimony as a statement against interest.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Recall the exceptions to hearsay. - Party to case exception applies only to parties, not witnesses. - Dying declaration requires the declarant to be on the brink of death. - Statement against interest requires the statement to be against the declarant's own interest. None apply. Therefore the testimony is hearsay and must be excluded. Full solution: The passenger is a third‑person witness; his statement does not fall under any statutory exception to the hearsay rule. Consequently, the court must exclude the testimony.

questions.text: The new government policy is a __________ for small businesses, as it provides essential financial support to keep them from collapsing during the economic downturn. A) A lifeline B) A tightrope C) A stepping-stone D) A dead-end

options.label: A
options.text: A lifeline

options.label: B
options.text: A tightrope

options.label: C
options.text: A stepping-stone

options.label: D
options.text: A dead-end

questions.solution: The phrase 'lifeline' refers to something that saves a person or organization from disaster, which perfectly matches the context of financial support preventing collapse. 'Tightrope' implies walking a dangerous path with little margin for error, not receiving help. 'Stepping-stone' suggests a means to progress to a higher goal, not immediate survival. 'Dead-end' indicates a situation with no future or success, which contradicts the supportive nature of the policy.
